text:
Tom (Sales): @Maya ACME POC hitting 403s on /v1/generate since yesterday. Sales call in 30m, can we triage quickly? error shows 'invalid_org_claim'.
ACME Dev: We used the onboarding key sent by email. curl below returns 403: 
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-Acme123456" -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"invalid_org_claim"}

Maya (Presales SE): Can you paste the full response headers and the token kid? also confirm whether the key string starts with sk- or sh- (shadow).
ACME Dev: Token id in logs: kid=9f3a7b. Key starts with sk-. Response headers incl: x-redwood-binding: tenant=acme-staging; policy=read-only
ACME Dev: Log line: authz: tenant_mismatch expected=acme-corp got=acme-staging. No project field included.
Sam (Backend): That log makes it pretty clear: the API key is bound to the acme-staging tenant. POC is calling with X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp so binding fails. Two routes: (1) issue org-scoped key, (2) update request to use the tenant the key is bound to, or (3) use a demo/key without tenant restriction for quick test.
Maya (Presales SE): Quick test you can run to confirm binding: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-Acme123456" https://api.redwood.example/v1/keys/introspect
```
Look for binding metadata in the body: {"kid":"9f3a7b","binding":"tenant=acme-staging","scopes":["generate"]}

ACME Dev: Introspect output shows binding exactly as Sam said. Oops — someone grabbed the staging key. We thought onboarding key would be prod-scoped.
Maya (Presales SE): I'll create a short-lived org-scoped key for the POC now. Note: for audit reasons we set default TTL to 24h for temporary keys. @Priya FYI for the security questionnaire.
Priya (Security): Agree on TTL. If we create an org-scoped POC key we need to limit scopes to generation only and add an expiry + explicit note in the security pack. Also confirm no prod data will be used.
Tom (Sales): Also customer asked about rate limits / pricing for high-throughput POC — they want to know if we can support 200 reqs/sec during demo and what Dedicated pricing would look like.
Sam (Backend): Default trial rate limit is 50 rps. For bursts to 200 rps we can spin a temporary dedicated pool but that requires sales ops approval. Rough estimate: POC burst add-on or short-term dedicated starts around the reserved baseline — I'll DM ops numbers.
Maya (Presales SE): Created temp key in the admin console, rotating now. Key id -> sk-temp-2287654321 (expires in 24h). Pasting for ACME over secure DM.
DeployBot: New key issued: sk-temp-2287654321, kid=zz9f3, expires=2024-12-01T14:00:00Z
ACME Dev: Re-tested with the new key and X-Redwood-Org: acme-corp header — 200 OK, generation works. Thanks! :tada:
Tom (Sales): Great — please add a note in the CRM that we provided org-scoped temp key and the TTL. ACME also wants the SOC2 + security packet before legal signs.
Priya (Security): I'll send the security packet + SOC2 link and a short checklist for the questionnaire. Also adding a note: any temp keys we issue for sales must be rotated after POC and logged in the key registry.
Maya (Presales SE): Follow-up actions: 1) rotate temp key at end of POC (24h TTL auto) 2) Sam to DM ops about burst pricing for 200 rps 3) Priya to send security pack 4) Tom to confirm CRM notes.
ACME Dev: We'll fill out the questionnaire today and confirm whether we need dedicated performance for the final demo. Thanks team!
Tom (Sales): Perfect — I'll keep the 11:30 call and update ACME that auth/keys resolved. :thumbsup:
